content: Medical direction, also referred to as online medical direction, is a process that enables a paramedic or an emergency medical technician (EMT) to communicate with a physician from the field using radio or other communication methods. This allows the paramedic or EMT to receive specific instructions regarding the continued care of a patient. This approach is particularly utilized when the required care exceeds the caregiver's authorized scope of practice without direct medical oversight. For instance, consider a scenario where a paramedic is managing a burn victim in the field. The paramedic may have already administered the maximum allowable dose of a narcotic pain reliever under their scope of practice. In such a case, the paramedic would attempt to contact their base station hospital to consult with a physician and obtain further instructions to provide additional pain relief for the patient. There are two distinct types of medical direction. The first is direct medical direction, commonly referred to as online medical direction. In this type, care is provided under the explicit orders of a base station physician, typically communicated via radio or telephone. The second type is indirect medical direction, also known as offline medical direction. This involves the creation of a set of pre-established written instructions, which are referred to as protocols. These protocols may also be termed standing orders.
